summary: This note covers the 1948 United States presidential election, the 41st quadrennial presidential election, held on Tuesday, November 2, 1948. Incumbent Democratic President Harry S. Truman defeated Republican Governor Thomas E. Dewey. The note describes Truman's win as one of the greatest election upsets in American history.
one_line: The 1948 US presidential election, in which incumbent Harry S. Truman defeated Republican Thomas E. Dewey in an upset.
key_facts: The 1948 United States presidential election was the 41st quadrennial presidential election.
The election was held on Tuesday, November 2, 1948.
Incumbent President Harry S. Truman was the Democratic nominee.
Harry S. Truman defeated Republican Governor Thomas E. Dewey.
Thomas E. Dewey was a Republican Governor.
Truman's victory is considered to be one of the greatest election upsets in American history.
